body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāgaṇapatistotra</s> (Great Hymn to <s>Gaṇapati</s>) composed by <s>Śrī Rāghavacaitanya</s>, accompanied by a commentary (<s>ṭippaṇī</s>) composed by his student.

children.translated_text: The <s>yoga</s> (meditation) of the knowers of <s>yoga</s>, whose minds, purified by the removal of various attachments, are the seats of meditation from which streams of nectar-essence have manifested,
overflowing with the fragrant splendor of sweet awakening, inundated with bliss — we worship that <s>Bhūman</s> (Infinite), who has manifested in the form of the elephant-faced one. || 1 ||

body.text:
dantāvalo gajastasyevāsyaṃ mukhaṃ yasya sa gajānanastadātmanā tadrūpeṇa pariṇataṃ taṃ bhūmānaṃ paraṃ brahmopāsmahe |
kīdṛśaṃ tam |
ānando brahmānandastena plavamānaḥ |
lakṣaṇayā pūrṇānandābhinna ityarthaḥ |
īdṛśo yo bodhastena cidānandamayaṃ svarūpamuktam |
tadvivartarūpaḥ prapañca eva madhurāmodacchaṭātvena rūpitastena meduram |

children.translated_text: Furthermore, what is it like?
[It is] the <s>yoga</s> of the knowers of <s>yoga</s>.
What are these knowers of <s>yoga</s> like?

children.text: vidhūto vividho vyāsaṅgo yairata eva śuddho ya āśayastasminprādurbhūtaḥ sudhārasaḥ śāntisukhaṃ yeṣāṃ te ca te prasṛmaraṃ prasāri dhyānaṃ yasminnīdṛśaṃ yadāspadaṃ kaṃdarādi tadadhyāsinaśca teṣām ||
children.translated_text: Those whose various attachments have been removed — hence whose minds are pure; in those [pure minds] the nectar-essence, the peace and happiness, has manifested; they are spreading; meditation is [directed toward] such a seat as a cave or the like; and they are seated in those [places of meditation].

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Dantāvala</s> means elephant; one whose face (<s>āsya</s>) is like that is the elephant-faced one (<s>Gajānana</s>); "in his form" means "in that appearance" — we worship that <s>Bhūman</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, who has manifested [thus]. What is he like? "Inundated with bliss" — <s>ānanda</s> means the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>; "floating" [in it]. By implication, the meaning is: identical with complete bliss. Such is the <s>bodha</s> (awareness); by this, the essential nature as consisting of consciousness and bliss is stated. The manifest universe, which is its apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>), is represented as a mass of sweet fragrance; by that it is overflowing.

children.text: tāraśrīparaśaktikāmavasudhārūpānugāṃ yaṃ vidustasmai stātpraṇatirgaṇādhipataye yo rāgiṇābhyarthyate /
children.translated_text: Him whom they know as [the deity whose mantra] follows the forms of <s>tāra</s> (Oṃ), <s>śrī</s>, <s>paraśakti</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>vasudhā</s> — to that Lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, may there be obeisance; who is entreated by the passionate one,

children.text: āmantrya prathamaṃ vareti varadetyārtena sarvaṃ janaṃ svāminme vaśamānayeti satataṃ svāhādibhiḥ pūjitaḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: having first addressed him as "<s>Vara</s>" (O excellent one), then as "<s>Varada</s>" (O bestower of boons), by the afflicted one [saying] to all people: "O Lord, bring [them] under my control" — [he who is] constantly worshipped with <s>svāhā</s> and other [mantric endings]. || 2 ||

body.text:
mahāgaṇapatimantramuddharati - tāraḥ praṇavaḥ, śrīrlakṣmībījam, paraśaktirmāyābījam, kāmaḥ kāmabījam, vasudhā bhūmibījam, iti pañcarūpāṇāṃ bījānāmanu gamityakṣarametādṛśaṃ yaṃ sādhakā vidustasmai gaṇādhipataye praṇatiḥ stāditi yojanā |
yaḥ satataṃ svāhāsvadhādibhiḥ śaktibhiḥ pūjitaḥ |
ārtena rāgiṇā prathamaṃ vareti tato varadetyāmantryābhyarthyate |
abhyarthanāmevāha - sarvaṃ janaṃ svāminme vaśamānayeti |

children.translated_text: By [the phrase] "with <s>svāhā</s> and others," the mantra ending in <s>svāhā</s> [is indicated].
Here the word "<s>adhi</s>" (over) and the word "<s>sarvam</s>" (all) are used to accommodate the metre.

children.text: mantre tu gaṇapataye tathā sarvajanamityekameva padam |
children.translated_text: But in the mantra, "<s>gaṇapataye</s>" and "<s>sarvajanam</s>" are indeed a single word each.
And "<s>svāmin</s>" (O Lord) is external to the mantra.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] He extracts the <s>Mahāgaṇapati mantra</s>: <s>tāra</s> is the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), <s>śrī</s> is the <s>Lakṣmī-bīja</s> (seed syllable of Lakṣmī), <s>paraśakti</s> is the <s>māyā-bīja</s>, <s>kāma</s> is the <s>kāma-bīja</s>, <s>vasudhā</s> is the <s>bhūmi-bīja</s> — thus the syllable that follows (<s>anu</s>) [i.e., accompanies] the seed syllables of these five forms — him whom the practitioners know in this way, to that Lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s> may there be obeisance — this is the construction. He who is constantly worshipped with the <s>śaktis</s> (powers) such as <s>svāhā</s>, <s>svadhā</s>, and others. By the afflicted, passionate one, having first addressed him as "<s>Vara</s>," then as "<s>Varada</s>," he is entreated. The entreaty itself is stated: "O Lord, bring all people under my control."

children.translated_text: In an ocean of sugarcane juice whose surface of waters is kissed by the edges of surging waves, on a jewel-made island, nourished solely by the fragrance of the groves of celestial wish-fulfilling trees,
at the root of a wish-fulfilling tree, on a throne of great gems, on an imperishable lotus, on the pericarp formed by a triangle set within a hexagram — I worship him. || 3 ||

children.text: kallolānāṃ mahormīṇāmañcalāḥ prāntāstairāśliṣṭā meghatatiryenaitādṛśa ikṣurasasamudre suradrumāṇāṃ pārijātādīnāṃ vanaṃ tadāmodena paripuṣṭe |
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The edges, i.e. the borders, of the <s>kallolas</s> (great waves) — embraced by them is the expanse of clouds; in such an ocean of sugarcane juice; nourished by the fragrance of the groves of <s>suradrumaas</s> (divine trees) such as <s>Pārijāta</s> and others.

children.text: ratnamayaṃ dvīpaṃ vārimadhyasthalaṃ tadgatasya kalpatarormūle mahāmaṇimayaṃ pīṭhaṃ tatra ṣaṭkoṇayuktatrikoṇakarṇīkāyukte 'kṣarāmbhoruhe tantraprasiddhe mātṛkākamale 'muṃ mahāgaṇapatiṃ bhaje ||
children.translated_text: A jewel-made island, a land in the midst of water; at the root of the wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpataru</s>) situated there, on a throne made of great gems, on an imperishable lotus — [that is,] on the lotus of the <s>Mātṛkā</s> letters well-known in the <s>Tantras</s> — fitted with a pericarp formed by a triangle set within a hexagram, I worship this <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>.
[Bearing in his hands] a discus, a trident, a sugarcane bow, a mace, a citron, his own tusk, a rice-shoot, a blue lotus, a noose, and a lotus; with a pot shining at the tip of his trunk,

children.text: āśliṣṭaṃ priyayā sarojakarayā ratnasphuradbhūṣayā māṇikyapratimaṃ mahāgaṇapatiṃ viśveśamāśāsmahe || 4 ||
children.translated_text: embraced by his beloved, whose lotus-hands [hold him], adorned with radiant jewels, resembling a ruby — we pray to <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>, the Lord of the universe. || 4 ||

children.text: cakraṃ prasiddham, prāsastriśūlaḥ, rasālakārmukamikṣudhanuḥ, gadā prasiddhā, bījapūro mātuliṅgam, dvijaḥ svakīyo dantaḥ, vrīhyagraṃ śālimañjarī, utpalaṃ prasiddham, pāśapaṅkaje ca prasiddhe, evaṃ daśāyudhāni kareṣu yasya |
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The discus (<s>cakra</s>) is well-known; the <s>prāsa</s> is a trident (<s>triśūla</s>); the <s>rasāla-kārmuka</s> is the sugarcane bow; the mace (<s>gadā</s>) is well-known; <s>bījapūra</s> is a citron (<s>mātuliṅga</s>); <s>dvija</s> ("twice-born") is his own tusk (<s>danta</s>); <s>vrīhyagra</s> is a rice-shoot (<s>śālimañjarī</s>); <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) is well-known; the noose (<s>pāśa</s>) and lotus (<s>paṅkaja</s>) are well-known — thus [he has] ten weapons in his hands.

children.text: śuṇḍāgre puṣkare jāgratsthito ghaṭo ratnapūrṇo hemakumbho yasya |
children.translated_text: At the tip of his trunk, on the lotus [ornament], there stands a pot — a golden vessel (<s>hemakumbha</s>) filled with gems.

children.text: kamalahastayā priyayā dakṣiṇahastenāliṅgitaṃ māṇikyapratimaṃ śoṇacchaviṃ sarveśvaraṃ mahāgaṇapatimāśāsmahe ||
children.translated_text: Embraced on the right side by his beloved, whose hand [holds] a lotus — resembling a ruby, i.e., of reddish complexion — we pray to <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>, the Lord of all.
Two laudatory [verses] in the guise of a pair of cheek-circles, reddened with vermilion, bearing hanging <s>rolamba</s> (garlands), swinging and spreading, overflowing with the waters of rut-fluid,

children.text: trailokyeṣṭāvidhānavarṇasubhagaṃ yaḥ padmarāgopamaṃ dhatte sa śriyamātanotu satataṃ devo gaṇānāṃ patiḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: He who bears [a form] beautiful in hue, [suited] for performing the desired rites of the three worlds, resembling a <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby)—may that god, the lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>, perpetually bestow prosperity. || 5 ||

children.text: dānāmbhasā madāmbunā parimeduraṃ vyāptaṃ prasṛmarānvyālambino rolambānbhramarānbibhartīti prasṛmaravyālambirolambabhṛt |
children.translated_text: Enveloped and saturated with the water of rut-ichor (<s>dāna-ambhas</s> = <s>mada-ambuna</s>), it bears the bees (<s>rolamba</s> = <s>bhramara</s>) that hang down crawling—thus [the compound] <s>prasṛmara-vyālambi-rolamba-bhṛt</s>.

Reddened by vermilion (<s>sindūra</s>), such a pair of temple-regions (<s>kumbha-pradeśa-dvaya</s>) of his—from the appearance of that, [the compound] '<s>trailokya-iṣṭa-vidhāna-varṇa-subhaga</s>' [means] charming, beautiful in hue like the imperishable auspicious script of the three worlds.

children.text: padmarāgopamaṃ padmarāgo lohitakastadupamaṃ praśastidvayaṃ yo dhatte sa gaṇānāṃ patirdevaḥ satataṃ śriyamātanotu |
children.translated_text: '<s>Padmarāga-upama</s>' — <s>padmarāga</s> is a ruby (<s>lohitaka</s>); '<s>tat-upama</s>' means resembling that. He who bears this twofold beauty (<s>praśasti-dvaya</s>)—that god, the lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>, may he perpetually bestow prosperity (<s>śrī</s>).

children.text: yathā mṛdambulipte dāruphalake raktacūrṇaṃ dattvākṣarāṇi, tathā dānāmbulipte sindūravati kumbhasthale bhramarā ityuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Just as letters [are formed] by placing red powder on a wooden board smeared with wet clay, so the bees [appear] on the temple-region smeared with ichor-water and marked with vermilion—this is what is stated.

[Those lustre-rays] whose true semblance is like the cascading wave-tips of the Milk Ocean (<s>Kṣīrābdhi</s>), rendered helpless by the spinning whirl of the revolving Mount <s>Mandara</s>, which drag away all the pride of the beauty of the interplay of waving <s>cāmaras</s> (chowries),

which are showers of pure camphor-and-sandalwood paste [reaching to] the ends of the quarters, which spread freely and pervade the sky—may those lustre-rays of <s>Heramba</s>'s (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>'s) tusks take refuge in [our] minds! || 6 ||

body.text:
herambadantatviṣo manaḥ śrayantām |
kiṃbhūtāḥ |
bhrāmyato mandarasya ghūrṇanāvṛttayastadāyattasya kṣīrābdhervīcayo laharyastāsāṃ chaṭā agrabhāgāstaiḥ sadṛśāḥ |
punaḥ kīdṛśāḥ |
calacāmaravyatikaraśrīgarvasarvaṃkakṛṣāḥ |
vyatikaro vyatiṣaṅgaḥ |

children.translated_text: '<s>Dikkānta</s>-' etc. is a metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>).
<s>Ghanasāra</s> means camphor (<s>karpūra</s>).
Likewise, '<s>svacchanda-prasara-pralipta-viyataḥ</s>' [means] whose considerable spread fills the sky.
By this, the abundance of the lustre-rays is expressed.

body.translated_text: 'May the lustre-rays of <s>Heramba</s>'s tusks take refuge in [our] minds.' Of what nature? The turnings of the revolving <s>Mandara</s>, the waves of the Milk Ocean dependent on it, the tips—the fore-parts—of those [waves]; resembling those. Again, of what nature? Those that drag away all the pride of the beauty of the interplay of waving chowries. <s>Vyatikara</s> means <s>vyatiṣaṅga</s> (intertwining).

children.translated_text: Beautiful with the clusters of radiance from heaps of rubies (<s>māṇikya</s>) that blossom forth, interspersed with a net of pearls (<s>muktā</s>); resembling coral (<s>pravāla</s>) that touches the dense fullness of masses of conch shells (<s>kambu</s>),

companions of twilight (<s>saṃdhyā</s>) that slowly churns the flood-waves of moonlight (<s>jyotsnā</s>)—the bodily lustre-rays of <s>Heramba</s>, pervaded by the radiance of his tusks, are forever triumphant! || 7 ||
Beautiful and enchanting like the clusters of radiance from heaps of blazing rubies mixed with masses of pearls.
Equal to coral spread widely and joined with masses of conch shells.

children.text: jyotsnāpūrataraṅge mantharaṃ tarantī cāsau saṃdhyā ca tasyā vayasyāḥ sāmyātsakhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃdhyā</s> (twilight), which slowly crosses the flood-waves of moonlight—its companions (<s>vayasya</s>), on account of similarity, are friends (<s>sakhī</s>).
Such bodily lustre-rays of <s>Heramba</s>, pervaded by the radiance of his tusks, are forever triumphant.

Honoring devotees (<s>sādhaka-jana</s>) by the crores, with a golden vessel (<s>hema-kalaśa</s>) held at the tip of his trunk, overturned and streaming [forth] with heaps of various gems (<s>ratna</s>),

playfully flapping his ears, which manifests as the driving away of bees greedy for the fragrance of his rut-ichor (<s>dāna</s>)—the god, the chief of the <s>gaṇas</s> (<s>gaṇa-grāmaṇī</s>), is victorious! || 8 ||

body.text: śuṇḍāpradhṛtasuvarṇakalaśasaṃgṛhītena kṣaratā bahutvādbahirapi nirgacchatā muktāmāṇikyādiratnasamūhena koṭiśaḥ sādhakajanānsaṃbhāvayannasaṃkhyātānupāsakānsaṃpadā vardhayan /
body.translated_text: With the mass of gems—pearls, rubies, and the like—held in the golden vessel grasped at the tip of the trunk, streaming out copiously, honoring devotees by the crores, enriching countless worshippers with prosperity.

children.translated_text: '<s>Dāna</s>-' etc. [is explained as follows]:
<s>Āmoda</s> [means both] fragrance and delight.
<s>Protsāraṇa</s> means driving away (<s>uccāṭana</s>); for that purpose, the play of ear-flapping manifests.
The god, the lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>, is victorious.

children.text: herambaṃ praṇamāmi yasya purataḥ śāṇḍilyamūle śriyā bibhratyāmburuhe samaṃ madhuripuste śaṅkhacakre vahan /
children.translated_text: I bow to <s>Heramba</s>, before whom, at the root of a <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> (<s>bilva</s>) tree, <s>Madhuripa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>), together with <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) bearing a lotus, stands holding the conch and discus,

children.text: nyagrodhasya tale sahādrisutayā śaṃbhustayā dakṣiṇe bibhrāṇaḥ paraśuṃ triśūlamitayā pāśāṅkuśābhyāṃ śubham || 9 ||
children.translated_text: and at the foot of a banyan tree (<s>nyagrodha</s>), on his right side, <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), together with the Daughter of the Mountain (<s>Adrisutā</s>, <s>Pārvatī</s>), holding the axe (<s>paraśu</s>) and trident (<s>triśūla</s>), auspicious, along with the noose (<s>pāśa</s>) and goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>). || 9 ||

children.text: śāṇḍilyamūle bilvavṛkṣasyādho yasya mahāgaṇapateḥ purato 'grabhāge padme bibhratyā śriyā samaṃ te prasiddhe śaṅkhacakre vahanmadhuripurviṣṇurasti |
children.translated_text: At the root of the <s>śāṇḍilya</s>, beneath the <s>bilva</s> tree, in the front portion of that <s>Mahā-Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Madhuripa</s>, that is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, stands together with <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) bearing a lotus, holding those well-known conch and discus.

children.text: tathā yasya dakṣiṇe nyagrodhasya tale vaṭavṛkṣādhaḥ pāśāṅkuśābhyāmitayā sahitayādrisutayā pārvatyā saha paraśuṃ triśūlaṃ ca bibhrāṇaḥ śaṃbhuḥ śivo 'sti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, on his right side, at the foot of the <s>nyagrodha</s>, beneath the banyan tree, <s>Śambhu</s>, that is <s>Śiva</s>, stands together with the Daughter of the Mountain (<s>Adrisutā</s>), that is <s>Pārvatī</s>, accompanied by [her] noose and goad, holding the axe and trident.

children.text: paścātpippalamāśrito ratipatirdevasya ratyotpale bibhratyā samamaikṣavaṃ dhanuriṣūnpauṣpānvahanpañca ca /
children.translated_text: Behind [him], resting at a sacred fig tree (<s>pippala</s>), <s>Ratipati</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>, the Lord of Love), together with <s>Rati</s> bearing a lotus, holding the sugarcane bow and five flower-arrows,

children.text: vāme cakragadādharaḥ sa bhagavānkroḍaḥ priyaṃgostale hastodyacchukaśālimañjarikayā devyā dharaṇyā saha || 10 ||
children.translated_text: and on the left, the blessed <s>Kroḍa</s> (<s>Varāha</s>, the Boar incarnation), bearing discus and mace, at the foot of a <s>priyangu</s> tree, together with the goddess <s>Dharaṇī</s> (Earth) holding up in her hand a parrot and a cluster of rice (<s>śāli-mañjarikā</s>). || 10 ||

body.text: devasya paścime pippalavṛkṣasyādha utpale bibhratyā ratyā samamaikṣavaṃ dhanuḥ pañca pauṣpāniṣūṃśca vahan ratipatiḥ kāmadevo 'sti /
body.translated_text: On the west of the deity, beneath a <s>pippal</s> tree, upon a lotus, together with <s>Rati</s> who bears [with him] a sugarcane bow and five flower-arrows — the husband of <s>Rati</s>, <s>Kāmadeva</s>, is [stationed].

body.text: asya ca vāme priyaṃguvṛkṣādho hastodyacchukaśālimañjarikayaikasminkare kīramanyatra kalamakaṇiśaṃ bibhratyā dharaṇyā saha sa prasiddho bhagavānkroḍo varāho 'sti taṃ herambaṃ praṇamāmīti pūrveṇānvayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And on his left, beneath a <s>priyaṅgu</s> tree, together with <s>Dharaṇī</s> (Earth) who holds up in her hands a parrot and a <s>śālī</s> rice-ear in one hand and a <s>kalama</s> grain-ear in the other — that renowned lord <s>Kroḍa</s>, i.e. <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar), is [stationed]. 'To him, <s>Heramba</s>, I bow' — this is the syntactic connection with the preceding [verse].

children.text: ṣaṭkoṇāśriṣu ṣaṭsu ṣaḍ gajamukhāḥ pāśāṅkuśābhīvarānbibhrāṇāḥ pramadāsakhāḥ pṛthumahāśoṇāśmapuñjatviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Verse:] On the six edges of the hexagon, six elephant-faced ones, bearing noose, goad, [the gesture of] fearlessness, and boons, accompanied by their consorts, with the radiance of great heaps of red gems —

children.text: āmodaḥ purataḥ pramodasumukhau taṃ cābhito durmukhaḥ paścātpārśvagato 'sya vighna iti yo vighnakarteti ca || 11 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āmoda</s> is in front, <s>Pramoda</s> and <s>Sumukha</s> on either side of him, <s>Durmukha</s> behind, at his side the one called <s>Vighna</s>, and the one called <s>Vighnakartā</s> (the obstacle-maker). [RMgan 11]

body.text:
ṣaṭkoṇasya pīṭhasya ṣaṭsvaśriṣu pālīṣu ṣaḍ gajamukhā dhyeyāḥ |
kīdṛśāste |
pāśāṅkuśābhayavarānhasteṣu bibhrāṇāḥ |
pramadānāṃ sakhāya iti pramadāsakhāḥ |
bhāryāsahitā ityarthaḥ |
pṛthuścāsau mahāśoṇāśmanāṃ padmarāgāṇāṃ puñjastadvattviṭ kāntiryeṣāṃ te |
yadi 'pṛthumahāḥ'; iti visargāntaḥ pāṭhastadā bhinnaṃ padam |
pṛthurmaho yeṣāṃ te |
akārānto 'pi mahaśabdo 'sti |
teṣāṃ nāmānyāha - purato 'grakoṇa āmodaḥ |
taṃ cāmodamabhitaḥ pramodasumukhau |

children.text: puraḥ kalpitapūrvadigapekṣayāgnikoṇe pramodaḥ, evamīśānakoṇe sumukha ityarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: With reference to the eastern direction imagined in front, <s>Pramoda</s> is in the <s>Agni</s> (southeast) corner; thus <s>Sumukha</s> is in the <s>Īśāna</s> (northeast) corner — this is the meaning.
Behind, in the western corner, is <s>Durmukha</s>.

children.text: asya durmukhasya vighna iti yasya nāma sa ekasminpārśve vighnakarteti yasya nāma sa dvitīyapārśve 'sti |
children.translated_text: The one named <s>Vighna</s> is at one side of this <s>Durmukha</s>; the one named <s>Vighnakartā</s> is at the second side.
That is to say, one is in the <s>Nairṛtya</s> (southwest) corner, the other is in the <s>Vāyavya</s> (northwest) corner.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] On the six edges (pālīs) of the hexagonal pedestal, six elephant-faced ones are to be meditated upon. What are they like? Bearing noose, goad, fearlessness, and boons in their hands. '<s>pramadāsakhāḥ</s>' means companions of beautiful women — that is, accompanied by their wives. '<s>pṛthu</s>' — great heaps of <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby) gems, whose radiance is like that. If the reading is '<s>pṛthumahāḥ</s>' with <s>visarga</s>, then it is a separate compound: those whose greatness is vast. The word '<s>maha</s>' also has an <s>a</s>-stem form. He states their names: in front, at the forward corner, is <s>Āmoda</s>. On either side of that <s>Āmoda</s> are <s>Pramoda</s> and <s>Sumukha</s>.

children.text: āmodādigaṇeśvarapriyatamāstatraiva nityaṃ sthitāḥ kāntāśleṣarasajñamantharadṛśaḥ siddhiḥ samṛddhistataḥ /
children.translated_text: [Verse:] The beloved consorts of <s>Āmoda</s> and the other <s>Gaṇeśvaras</s>, always dwelling there, with languid glances knowing the pleasure of their beloved's embrace — <s>Siddhi</s>, <s>Samṛddhi</s>, then —

children.text: kāntiryā madanāvatītyapi tathā kalpeṣu yā gīyate sānyā yāpi madadravā tadaparā drāviṇyamūḥ pūjitāḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kānti</s>, and she who is called <s>Madanāvatī</s>, likewise she who is celebrated in the <s>Kalpas</s>, and also <s>Madadravā</s>, and another <s>Drāviṇī</s> — these are worshipped. [RMgan 12]

children.text: kāntasya svasvabharturāliṅganarasaṃ jānantyata eva mantharā rāgiṇī dṛgyāsāṃ tāḥ |
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Those whose eyes are languid (<s>rāgiṇī</s>), knowing the pleasure of the embrace of their own respective husbands.

children.text: āmodādīnāṃ pūrvaślokoktānāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ bhāryāsteṣāṃ samīpe sthitā dhyeyāḥ |
children.translated_text: The wives of <s>Āmoda</s> and the other six mentioned in the previous verse — they are to be meditated upon as dwelling near them.

children.text: tāsāṃ nāmāni ca - siddhiḥ, samṛddhiḥ, kāntiḥ, madanāvatī, madadravā, drāviṇī ceti ||
children.translated_text: And their names are: <s>Siddhi</s>, <s>Samṛddhi</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Madanāvatī</s>, <s>Madadravā</s>, and <s>Drāviṇī</s>.

children.text: āśliṣṭau vasudhetyatho vasumatī tābhyāṃ sitālohitau varṣantau vasu pārśvayorvilasatastau śaṅkhapadmau nidhī /
children.translated_text: [Verse:] Embraced by <s>Vasudhā</s> and then by <s>Vasumatī</s>, white and red respectively, raining wealth on either side, those two shine — <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padma</s>, the two <s>Nidhis</s> (treasures).

children.text: aṅgānyanvatha mātaraśca paritaḥ śakrādayo 'bjāśrayāstadbāhye kuliśādayaḥ paripatatkālānalajyotiṣaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>aṅgas</s> (auxiliary [mantras]), and the <s>Mātṛs</s> (mothers) all around, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and others seated on lotuses; beyond them, the thunderbolt (<s>kuliśa</s>) and others, with the radiance of blazing <s>kālānala</s> (the fire of dissolution). [RMgan 13]

body.text: vasudhayā vasumatyā ca krameṇāliṅgitau śuklaraktavarṇau dhanaṃ varṣantau tau śaṅkhapadmasaṃjñau prasiddhau nidhī ṣaṭkoṇapārśvayorvilasataḥ /
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Embraced by <s>Vasudhā</s> and <s>Vasumatī</s> respectively, white and red in color, raining wealth — those two famous treasures known as <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padma</s> shine on either side of the hexagon.

children.translated_text: One should meditate upon them — this is the meaning.
After (<s>anu</s>) meditating on the <s>Nidhis</s>, one should meditate on the six <s>aṅgas</s> (auxiliary mantras) [corresponding to] the heart and so forth.
All around, the eight <s>Mātṛs</s> (mothers) beginning with <s>Brāhmī</s> are to be meditated upon.

children.text: ṣaṭkoṇādbahiḥsthite 'ṣṭadalakamala indrādayo dikpālāstadbāhye teṣāṃ samīpa eva paripatatkālānalajyotiṣaḥ pradīptasvarūpā indrādīnāṃ hetayo vajrādyā dhyeyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the eight-petaled lotus situated outside the hexagon, <s>Indra</s> and the other <s>Dikpālas</s> (guardians of the directions) [are to be meditated upon]; beyond them, in their very vicinity, the weapons of <s>Indra</s> and others — the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) etc. — blazing in form like the fire of dissolution (<s>kālānala</s>), are to be meditated upon.

[Verse:] Thus, to <s>Śrī Vakratuṇḍa</s> (the crooked-trunked one, i.e. <s>Gaṇeśa</s>), whose body is the essence of the <s>tattvas</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and others, who has scattered the entire host of <s>Daitya</s> armies by [his] <s>Huṃkāra</s>, whose radiance is blazing —

In whom the waves of all [modifications] have been destroyed by the surge of awakening to the sole essence of bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), to that supreme one — the first, enchanting radiance everywhere — to him, the highest, homage! [RMgan 14]

body.text:
'herambaṃ praṇamāmi'; (9/10) iti ślokābhyāṃ viṣṇuśivādisvarūpaistanurmūrtiryasya sa tasmai |
ādipadātsmarakroḍau |
huṃkāramātreṇa nirastasamastāsurasainyasamūhāya dīptakāntaye |
ānandeti |
niratiśayasukhasphuraṇataraṅgairdūrīkṛtasaṃpūrṇormaye |
ūrmayaḥ ṣaḍbhāvavikārāḥ |

children.text: te ca - jāyate, asti, vardhate, vipariṇamate, apakṣīyate, naśyatīti ca |
children.translated_text: And they are: being born (<s>jāyate</s>), existing (<s>asti</s>), growing (<s>vardhate</s>), transforming (<s>vipariṇamate</s>), declining (<s>apakṣīyate</s>), and perishing (<s>naśyati</s>).

children.text: ānandaikarasāvayodhalaharībhirvidhvastāḥ sarveṣāṃ sādhakānāmūrmayaḥ ṣaḍindriyajanyā vṛttayo yasmādityeke |
children.translated_text: By the waves of the ocean whose sole essence is <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), destroyed are all the practitioners' (<s>sādhakas'</s>) waves—that is, the mental modifications (<s>vṛttis</s>) born of the six senses—thus say some.
By the word 'waves' (<s>ūrmi</s>) [are meant] the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) such as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and so forth, well-known in the <s>Yoga śāstras</s>.

children.text: sarvatra prathamānaṃ mugdhaṃ sundaraṃ maho yasya tasmai parasmai jagato 'nyasmai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Obeisance to that supreme one, other than the world, whose splendor (<s>mahas</s>) is everywhere foremost, captivating, and beautiful.

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] By the two verses '<s>herambaṃ praṇamāmi</s>' (vv. 9-10), [the meaning is:] to him whose body (<s>tanu</s>/<s>mūrti</s>) consists of the forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and others. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), <s>Smara</s> (<s>Kāma</s>) and <s>Kroḍa</s> (<s>Varāha</s>) [are also included]. To him whose entire army of <s>Asuras</s> has been repelled by a mere <s>Huṃkāra</s>, whose radiance is blazing. '<s>Ānanda</s>': by the waves of the dawning of unsurpassed bliss, the complete <s>ūrmis</s> (modifications) have been removed. The <s>ūrmis</s> are the six modifications of being (<s>ṣaḍ-bhāva-vikāras</s>).

children.translated_text: Of those—gods, demons, and hosts of humans eager in devoted service—whose innumerable blazing crown-tips are adorned with streams of radiance from rows of jewels equal to the sun,

children.text: rājannīrājanaśrīsakhacaraṇanakhadyotavidyotamānaḥ śreyaḥ stheyaḥ sa deyānmama vimaladṛśo bandhuraṃ sindhurāsyaḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: he, the elephant-faced one (<s>sindhurāsya</s>), resplendent with the radiance of his toenails that are companions to the beauty of the shining <s>nīrājana</s> (lamp-waving ceremony)—may he grant me, of pure vision, beautiful and steadfast blessings. (RMgan 15)

body.text:
sevāyāṃ hevāko 'bhilāṣo yeṣām |
ahamagre 'hamagre bhavāmītīcchā |
ahaṃpūrviketi yāvat |
te ca te devāsuranarāṇāṃ samūhāsteṣāṃ dedīpyamānamukuṭāgrāṇāṃ yā koṭiḥ saṃkhyāviśeṣastatra vyāṭīkamānāḥ susaṃgatāḥ sūryatulyaratnapaṅktikāntipravāhāsteṣām |
rājantī nīrājanaśrīrārātrikaśobhā tasyāḥ sakhāyaste ca te caraṇanakhāśca teṣāṃ dyotena prakāśena vidyotamānaḥ sa prasiddhaḥ sindhurāsyo gajamukhaḥ |

children.translated_text: O 'pure-eyed ones' (<s>vimaladṛśaḥ</s>), [meaning] the learned ones (<s>paṇḍitāḥ</s>).

children.text: mama bandhuraṃ ramyaṃ stheyaḥ sthirataraṃ śreyaḥ kalyāṇaṃ deyāt |
children.translated_text: May he grant me beautiful (<s>bandhura</s>), delightful (<s>ramya</s>), most steadfast (<s>stheyas</s>), and auspicious (<s>kalyāṇa</s>) welfare (<s>śreyas</s>).
Or, '<s>vimaladṛśaḥ</s>' (of pure vision) is a qualifier of 'mama' (my/me).

children.text: 'vimaladṛśā'; iti pāṭhe tu saumyāvalokanena śreyo dadyādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the reading '<s>vimaladṛśā</s>' (with pure gaze), the meaning is: may he grant welfare through his gentle glance.

body.translated_text: '<s>Hevāka</s>' means desire in service—the wish 'Let me be first, let me be first'; meaning 'each vying to be foremost' (<s>ahaṃpūrvikā</s>). And they are the hosts of gods, demons, and humans; of the tips of their blazing crowns, the innumerable [gems] therein are well-arranged, [forming] streams of radiance from rows of jewels equal to the sun. The shining beauty of the <s>nīrājana</s> is the <s>āratrika</s> (lamp-waving) splendor; its companions are those toenails, and illuminated by their radiance, he is the well-known <s>sindhurāsya</s>, [meaning] the elephant-faced one (<s>gajamukha</s>).

children.translated_text: By this hymn (<s>stava</s>), which contains within it a garland of manifest and secret <s>mantras</s>, and which is of very clear understanding (<s>sphuṭatarasaṃvid</s>),

children.text: yaḥ stauti pracurataraṃ mahāgaṇeśaṃ tasyeyaṃ bhavati vaśaṃvadā trilokī || 16 ||
children.translated_text: he who praises <s>Mahāgaṇeśa</s> most abundantly—for him, this triple world becomes obedient. (RMgan 16)
By [the compound] '<s>sphuṭatarasaṃvid</s>' (of very clear understanding), the quality of <s>prasāda</s> (clarity/grace) in the hymn is indicated.
'<s>Pracurataraḥ</s>' (most abundantly) [means] again and again.
The rest is clear.

body.text: || iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryavaryaśrīrāghavacaitanyaviracitaṃ mahāgaṇapatistotraṃ tacchiṣyakṛtayā ṭippaṇyā sametaṃ samāptam ||
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the <s>Mahāgaṇapatistotra</s> composed by the revered <s>Śrī Rāghavacaitanya</s>, the foremost among the <s>paramahaṃsa</s> wandering ascetics (<s>parivrājakācārya</s>), together with the commentary (<s>ṭippaṇī</s>) composed by his disciple.
